newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps all weaken bar fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps all weaken bar fuel oil.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly weaker on Wednesday except for heavy fuel.
Brent crude CFDs lost up to seven cents a barrel while gasoline slipped $3 a tonne and naphtha came off $2 a tonne. Heavy fuel gained $1. Middle distillate swaps focused on heavy selling of 4Q EN590.

Brent CFDs extended losses. The balance of this week sold at July Brent -43 cents while June 9-13 was concluded twice at -42 cents. Further out June 16-20 went at August -51 cents, roughtly equivalent to -42/43 under July.

Heavy fuel saw June trade at $84, $84.25 and $84.50 while low sulphur was pegged steady around $92 for June. Traders said fuel oil was not depressed by crude's recent weakness because the product was not bolstered when crude strengthened three weeks ago.

Gasoline swaps traded three times at $203, off about $2 from Tuesday and July was concluded at $194.50 once. Physical barges sold at $202 full ARA and $204 and $204.50 AR and also at $207, although most dealers said the latter deal was over the market and not reflective.
EN590 had a busy day with over 100,000 tonnes done on 4Q at $10.50 with one seller doing five deals to a variety of buyers. Dealers said prompt was around $7.
The gas oil crack spread was traded at $4.75 while 1Q98 was valued around $4.77 from $4.60 earlier in the day.
Some airline buying of 4Q jet was also seen around $27 and $27.50. June jet was under pressure with bids down to $17.50 although sellers were trying to hold onto $19.
Naphtha had a quiet day with traders assessing values about $2 lower with June at $183.50 and July $184.50.
